observation_summary: The FastDateFormat class failed to use the configured locale when initializing the Calendar object used for formatting dates, leading to incorrect week-of-year values.
hypothesis: The FastDateFormat.format(Date) method fails to use the locale stored in the FastDateFormat instance when creating the GregorianCalendar, causing it to default to the system locale's calendar rules (like firstDayOfWeek), which leads to incorrect week-of-year calculations.
prediction: The source code for FastDateFormat.format(Date) will show 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone)' instead of 'new GregorianCalendar(mTimeZone, mLocale)'.
experiment_rationale: The bug report and the nature of the failure (incorrect week calculation depending on locale) strongly point to an initialization error where the locale is ignored during calendar creation.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves passing the mLocale field to the GregorianCalendar constructor. This is a classic initialization error where a required state (the locale) was not used to initialize a dependent object (the calendar).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The logic for calculating the week is correct; the issue is simply that the wrong calendar instance (initialized with the wrong locale) is being used.
There is no missing guard or predicate; the issue is the state of the object being used for the calculation.
